=== ORDERING TRAP: CHECKED SPECIFICALLY, AND IT DOES NOT BITE ===
My dispatch warns that HANDOFF.md's generated block records a proof-record COUNT, and that if the generator runs before a commit that adds a proof record the count goes stale one commit later. The generator here (bc6874c) is NOT the last write: 46b2fd7 and a0f9481 come after it. I checked rather than assumed, and the count survives because both later commits are RENAMES (proof/41.json -> 42 -> 43), which hold the count constant at 21. Measured: the block says "21/21 proven" and `ls proof/*.json` minus schema/exempt is exactly 21.

MUTATION-PROBE, because a count that merely happens to match proves nothing about whether anything checks it:
  - set the block to "20/20 proven" while 21 records exist -> lwb_check_state_claims.py rc 1, "FAIL: [stale deliverable proof state in generated block] recorded=['20/20 proven'] re-derived=['21/21 proven']".
  - add a 22nd proof record leaving the block at 21 -> rc 1, "recorded=['21/21 proven'] re-derived=['22/22 proven']".
Both directions detected. The guard is real, not vacuous. Note for the next reader, since it cost me time: `lwb_handoff.py --check` passes in BOTH mutated cases -- it is not the script that checks the count. `lwb_check_state_claims.py` is.

=== FINDING 1 (NON-BLOCKING, REPRODUCED). A CARRIED-FORWARD SCOPED CLAIM IS NOW FALSE AS STATED. ===
reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md says, of the all-records bypass:
  "...resolve_reviewable_head skips record-only commits, so the head a record must attest to is the *base* commit, which the pull request does not modify."
  "**This pull request is itself an instance.**"
That was true of PR #32, where the document originated and where the PR really was all-records. It is NOT true of PR #43 as literally written. Measured: four of this PR's twelve commits (bc6874c, 1e622e3, 7be56dd, 8192011) touch HANDOFF.md and are therefore not record-only; the reviewable head is bc6874c, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor bc6874c bfe8507` is FALSE, i.e. bc6874c is a commit THIS PR ADDS, not the base commit. lwb-lanes accordingly does demand a review record naming a commit this PR introduces -- it failed for exactly that reason before this record landed.
This is the shape my dispatch tells me to hunt and the shape this repository keeps hitting: a claim true in one scope restated verbatim where the scope has changed. It is the third pass over this same document (df0de55, then b224d1b "the correction document made the same error it corrects"), so I am recording it precisely rather than letting it ride.
SUGGESTED CORRECTION, one sentence: say that this PR's *own content under reviews/ and proof/* is not covered by the gate -- which is true and which I prove below -- rather than that the PR is an all-records instance whose reviewable head is the base commit, which is not.

So the central deliverable of this PR can be rewritten to say anything at all, after an AGREE is filed, without moving the reviewable head or disturbing the gate. The document's conclusion stands exactly as written; only its account of the mechanism (Finding 1) is wrong for this PR.

=== WHY THIS IS AGREE AND NOT DISAGREE ===
I weighed blocking and decided against it, and I want the reasoning on the record rather than just the verdict. The deliverable is a correction record for a false provenance claim on #27. Its central subject -- that #27's reviewer run was hand-fired at 13:59:25Z against a `23 * * * *` cron, corroborated independently from GitHub's own clock -- is evidenced, and the record does not amend the landed #27 record, which is the right call. proof/43.json is unusually honest: `checked_by` is the literal string UNCHECKED-pending-independent-review, token accounting is recorded as "unknown" with an explicit refusal to borrow a number from another record, and its `unproven` list names the structural hole, the gate's inability to verify the central claim, and the fact that the six recorded commands are Windows-only. Every other gate is green and this branch repairs a state-claims failure main is currently carrying. Finding 1 is one inaccurate sentence in a self-referential aside whose operative advice I independently verified as correct; Finding 2 confirms the document's conclusion rather than undermining it. Blocking would cost another cycle in a re-cut chain that has already consumed #30, #35, #37, #38, #41 and #42, for a one-sentence documentation correction. Someone weighing this repository's standard on scoped claims more strictly than I do could reasonably call Finding 1 blocking; I am recording it prominently so that call remains available rather than buried.
A note the author can use: because reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md is a record-only path, correcting that sentence does NOT move the reviewable head and does NOT require a re-cut. It also, per Finding 2, will not re-trigger review -- so if the sentence is corrected, say so in the PR thread rather than relying on the gate to notice.

=== A NEAR-MISS I AM PRINTING RATHER THAN HIDING ===
I twice came within one command of filing a false accusation on this PR.
a. I first ran the count mutation-probes in a `git clone` of the local checkout and concluded that NOTHING verifies the proof count -- both probes "passed". Two things were wrong at once: the clone's origin/main resolved to 9b374b5, not the live bfe8507, so its state-claims baseline was not comparable; and I was reading `$?` after a pipeline, which gave me `tail`'s exit status rather than the script's, so every check looked like rc 0. Re-run in a faithful worktree with real exit codes, both probes FAIL correctly. Had I filed it, I would have charged a correct gate with being vacuous -- on the strength of a broken measurement, which is the precise "cannot tell 'I checked and found nothing' from 'I could not check'" failure my dispatch tells me to hunt. I had it myself.
b. proof/43.json declares `"commit": "3509d2f"`. `git cat-file -t 3509d2f` in my clone returns "fatal: Not a valid object name", and I was ready to report a proof record pointing at a commit that does not exist. Before writing it I queried the GitHub REST API: the commit IS real (3509d2fd12ff37d6d4e9c5acef7716755eeca74a) -- it simply lives on PR #32's closed, unmerged branch, which a fresh clone does not fetch. A missing object in MY clone is not a missing commit. Recorded as an observation instead, below, not a fault.
